body.p: Sylcha-Pylcha.[OSV:] The name SÉ¨lÊ¼ÄÊ¼a-PÉ¨lÊ¼ÄÊ¼a can be interpreted: (1) as an onomatopoeia, resembling birds' singing: cf. 'ilÊ¼ÄÊ¼a-pilÊ¼ÄÊ¼a' for ousel's cry (Taz), verbs 'sÄ±lÊ¼É¨mpÉ¨qo' - 'to ring', 'sÄ±lÊ¼qÉ¨mpÉ¨qo' - 'to squeak', 'pÄ±lÊ¼qÉ¨mpÉ¨qo' - 'to ring, to squeak'; There lived Sylcha-Pykcha Kash. He had got a mother.(2) from verbs 'pÉ¨lÊ¼ÄÊ¼É¨qo' - 'to mature, to ripen' and 'sÄ±lÊ¼tÉ¨qo' - 'be noisy', so that it could mean "a naughty grown-up". He didn't have a father. So he lived and lived. Once he said so to his mother, to his mother he said so then: "I'll go look for people.[OSV:] The nominal form "ÄÊ¼ontotÉ¨" has been edited into "ÄÊ¼ontot". How are we going to live so? Mother, don't you know [some] people in this area? His mother says: "I don't know any people. There are no people in this area near here." The son says like this to his mother: "You, he says, live here alone. I'll go look for [some] people soon." Then Sylcha-Pylcha Kash went through this area. Sylcha-Pylcha Kash went for a long time. Winter and summer passed by. He crossed the big river [Taz], he crossed small rivers. There were no people there. He went through the lakes, through the rivers. He was covered with snow from his cap on the forehead to his waist. Once he came to a forest, to a big forest. A river was passing through this forest. I went along the bank of this river. Once he hears something: ah plump!, ah plump! He walks and he hears such a voice. There is no animal, nobody there. He walked around this place: "Come on, who is speaking there? I would have a look at him." He walks and he walks. Still as if [something] is heard from down the river, [someone] is crying again: "Ah plump!, ah plump!" Such a sound echos apparently. He walks. Down the river, in the middle of the river something shows black. That foreigner is crying: "Ah plumps!, ah plumps!" Only not a human voice is crying like this. He came there. Apparently, a man was crying. He just came there, he gave a look: this is a man, a naked man in his bare skin [lit. with the meat of his father and his mother]. This naked man in his bare skin [lit. with the meat of his father and his mother] is sitting at the ice hole. Whether it was this man who had cried? "Why are you sitting here like that?" "No, he says, I sit here in order for the devil to eat me. There are my people on the bank. They made me sit here, so that the devil could eat me. If I leave [OSV:] The verbal form "omtÉ¨-ltÉ¨-mpÉË-tet" (sit.down-TR-PST.NAR-3PL) would be more correct here.simply so, the devil wil eat all of us, nobebody will stay [alive]. That's why they made me seat here. Go to the bank". "You go to the bank too." "How can I go away? The people will see me." "I tell you, go out." They went out to the bank. Sylcha-Pylcha Kash made an idol with his pike (he carved a human fase on the tree). "Don't you say anything about me! The devil will ask you, where did Sylcha-Pylcha go. Don't tell him anything about me." So he threatened him with his pike. He went to the bank and he saw there an earth-house. He made an idol (carved a face) there in the door opening as well. "Enter the house. Why do you stand there freezing?" "If I come in, my people will see me. You only come in." He made an idol (carved a face) in this door opening as well. "Don't you tell anything about me!" He threatened him with his pike. Nevertheless that man did come in. And everyone still saw him. Why do you come in, they say. "No, he says, this man sent me into the house. Some man came and sent me into the house. He brought me to the bank." He could hardly see: one more naked man appeared at the front side of the door. Then he said like this: "Dress this man." Then he went out and started listening, when the devil would appear from under the water. "If the devil appears, come into the house. Let one man listen." It is said, that when the evening dawn covers [the sky], then [the devil] goes out (appears). (probably at midnight) Enough time passed, once a man went out. It is said, [the] devil appears in the morning. [This man] ran into the house. "The devil is appearing! And you, he says, sit quietly, don't you dare coming out." Sylcha-Pylcha Kash is listening, what is [there]. He goes out onto the bank. He sees a hazel-hen. The hazel-hen: tweet-tweet. "Where did Sylcha-Pylcha go?" - "Sylcha-Pylcha has just left." He comes to the bank and he sees a [carved human] face. A [carved human] face says: "Sylcha-Pylcha sits at home." The devil, having turned to the bank, ran (went) [away], and fell into the water. As if glug [into the water]. Having run out, that Sylcha-Pylcha Kash chopped and broke the [carved human] face, and threw it away. He made another [carved human] face. He threatened the face: "You should never say anything about me!" Then he went out at dawn. Then they sit the whole night. At dawn they sent a man to have a look, whether [the devil] was coming out. They sent Sylcha-Pylcha Kash: "Listen." The man spent some time [there] quietly, [then] he ran into the house. The devil appeared, he said. The devil appeared. Sylcha-Pylcha heard it supposedly himself. [The devil] comes out onto the bank. He comes walking, he comes walking. He goes onto the top of that hill. He approaches that [carved human] face. Tweet-tweet, tweet-tweet, he says. "Where did Sylcha-Pylcha go, is he at home?" - "Sylcha-Pylcha has just left. You go to the bank, eat some food." That [devil] went walking, he approached the door opening, he approached the [carved human] face. "Where did [Sylcha-Pylcha] go?" - "Sylcha-Pylcha Kash, he went away (left) yesterday. Enter the house, eat some food." Once the devil pushed [himself] (started entering) into the house, he pushed [himself] (started entering) into the house. The devil had just come in, Sylcha-Pylcha Kash cut off his head. It rolled forward through the house. The body fell back outwards. He killed [the devil]. That Sylcha-Pylcha Kash brought the body out of the house. When he came out, it was already daytime. Sylcha-Pylcha brought the body [down] to the water, and put it into the ice hole. He made it freeze with ice, he put it like this. He put it like this near the ice hole. [The devil] lies as if he were alive. He put it sticking up with his head. We spent a day. It got dark. It is said, there are two [of them], we dont' know whether the other one can walk. In the evening it got dark . In the evening they are sitting for some time. It started getting dark. They send a man outwards: "Listen!" The man stands outside. "Oh! A man is appearing!" He ran into the house. Having entered the house, he said like this: "The devil is coming from under the water. He goes walking onto the bank." - "Who is coming onto the bank? Ah! Did you grow numb, did you overeat, did you get frightened?" [The devil] saw someone. "Earlier I used to lie down, having eaten." Then he went walking upwards. He came walking upwards. "Tweet-tweet. [?] Where did Sylcha-Pylcha Kash [OSV:] In the manuscript there is note to 4.31 that it was a sound of kissing, so the possible interpretation is that the devil kissed the idol before asking it about SylÊ¼cha-PylÊ¼cha.go? Did he go away or where did he go?" - "Sylcha-Pylcha had left earlier, he went away then. You go to the bank and eat some food." Then he went onto the bank and came to that [carved human] face. He said: "Is Sylcha-Pylcha at home?" "He left lately then. Come in, eat some food." That other one again like this: "Should I enter the house or should I not?" - the other one [said] again something. "Face, are you confusing me?" He is like hesitating, should he enter the house or should he not. Once he started entering [the house]. He had just pushed his head into the house, Sylcha-Pylcha Kash cut his head off. [The head] rolled forward into the house. The body fell back outwards. He killed [the devil]. Then they sit, and sit, noone [is coming]. Whether two [of them] are walking [there]? Next morning it started getting light. Chop firewood, he says. They chop firewood. "Set the fire." They really chop firewood. They brought both of them to the fire and burnt them, they burnt them completely on the fire. There was an old father with his child(ren), this old man had a daughter. He gave this daughter to Sylcha-Pylcha Kash. He went around the earth and came to the Selkups. That's the end.
